name: Pop-Out Plug Door
description: A sealed flat door that a cam lever pushes 40 mm off its gasket, then slides sideways along the outside of the wall on an overhead rail: no swing space, no floor track.
how_it_works: Closed, the flat door is squeezed against a rubber gasket all round, so it is draughtproof and quiet.
Lift the red cam lever 90 degrees. A cam behind the wall turns that rotation into a 40 mm straight push, moving the rail and the door outward.
The door has now left the gasket, so nothing rubs when it moves: that is why it seals better than a normal sliding door.
Pull the bar sideways; two roller trolleys carry the weight along the rail and a pin in the floor groove stops the bottom swinging.
The door parks against the wall beside the opening, leaving a full 900 mm step-free gap.
Lever down: the cam pulls the door back onto the gasket. Same idea as train and aircraft plug doors.
assumptions: Cam/bell-crank behind the wall is simplified to the lever's follows link.
Door is shown closed at rest; pop first (lever), then slide.
Wall is 100 mm; rail passes through guide blocks.
